barCharacter: Liam de Lioncourt (Monster Prom). He is the closest comic job: the most formal, most grammatical speaker in the cast, who claims taste authority and gives himself away in the act of sounding clever (the 180/360 line). Note: the corpus holds only about 8 Liam-spoken lines, so his 12 include two player options written in his orbit and narration about him.

ours12: Easily. My helm alone cost a fortune, from the finest bucket maker in Kent.
A wince. I have been winced at by a queen.
I challenged the little red clerk who underlineth my words to a duel. He underlined the challenge.
Grandly, for she took holy orders the very morning after my sonnet cycle.
{star} loathes {card}, so I have struck it from the ode, which is now a title.
Whoever calleth thee cute, a word for lambs, when thou art plainly the Great Fire of London.
I have drawn up {rival}'s elegy in advance, as a courtesy, with a space for the dates.
Choose me, and all thy virtues I shall prove. In sixteen hundred, that rhymed with love.
{card} offendeth {star}, and I, who invented {card}, hereby disown it.
I summon the barber to bleed the black bile from thee, and, since he is there, a fringe.
Remember me, if thou rememberest aught, as tall.
To the frost fair on the frozen river. Thou must find me a frozen river.
bar12: Maybe doing a 180 degree spin from cliches is good, but embracing cliches is like... making a 360 degree spin from them! So disruptive!
You! Save me from the consequences of my actions! Suggest an idea that lives up to my own hype!
Please, friend, help me find an unpopular band to worship until pop culture inevitably ruins it.
Ugh- I have no reason to care about this, but suddenly it's all I care about! Someone stop this madness!
What kind of status could I post that would be idiot-proof?
Yes, we have indeed encountered a culinary block. Perhaps you can suggest something appropriately artistic?
But I was sighing deeply because I couldn't help but think: supposing I were to actually acquire such a machine, I wonder...where in time would I go?
3.85 billion BC, so you can be into existing before it was cool.
Liam vanishes in a cloud of mist and angst.
Later, you see Liam beaming to himself. Liam? Beaming?
Liam de Lioncourt (4XX), a hipster vampire whose stand-offish demeanor hid that he was truly a lovable dork.
Well, I guess I'll be going then, because there's no way anyone could ever be as cool as Liam.
headToHead.voice: tie. Covered, Quill is identifiable in all 12, but much of that is costume (thee, hath, -eth) rather than shape. His one true shape, the serene boast whose proof gives him away (bucket maker, queen, holy orders), is as recognisable as Liam's formal-clause-then-plea. Strip the archaic verbs from the bank and about a third of it stops being Quill; strip the topic words from Liam and the plea-plus-self-betrayal still reads as Liam.
headToHead.construction: tie. Our top 12 are tighter than Liam's (his #7 runs 27 words and the culinary-block and status lines barely turn). The bucket maker in Kent, the underlined challenge and the struck card that leaves only a title all land on their last words. But each of Liam's best lines also exposes his want through a demand ('help me find', 'Suggest an idea'). Only about 6 of our 132 lines ask for anything; the rest are reports.
headToHead.quotable: bar. 'into existing before it was cool' and the 360-degree spin are lines that define the character, and fans repeat them. Our clip candidates (bucket maker in Kent, winced at by a queen, He underlined the challenge) are good gags, but none of them sums up who Quill is the way the 360 line sums up Liam.

templates: THE FLEEING MUSE (12 lines): my verse drove a woman or listener away, and I read the flight as tribute. Stable, holy orders, 'at a gallop', duchess fled, 'nunnery or a stable', 'summoned me twice', 'the infant wept', 'ladies lacking an ear', 'yawned during mine ode', 'winced at by a queen', the milkmaid who left the pastoral, '{card} the old thief that took every muse'. This is one anecdote told twelve ways. Keep two.

THE ODE IS ONLY A TITLE (8 lines): 'ending followeth by pigeon', 'gloriously begun, its title chosen', 'awaiteth only its last line', 'as of this moment, titled', 'which is now a title', 'an ode on {card} begun', 'Our first line is written', 'four hundred lines... Line one.' The secret is spent long before an episode ends.

THE RIVAL IS PROSE (10 lines): every insult falls back on scansion: 'speak prose in front of me', 'neither scans', 'such as cannot scan', 'be forever prose', 'apologise on behalf of prose', 'thick with plain speaking', 'plain sentences... laying bricks', 'rhymes with lunch', 'calleth moonlight nice', 'rhymed fire with desire'.
THE OVERDRESSED CLAUSE COLLAPSING ONTO 'hello' (2 lines, the same construction exactly): the sundials opener and the tapers-guttering one-on-one opener.
Repeated tags: 'and in Latin' twice (parent, comeback); 'Michaelmas' twice (three-words, Vex wingman); 'upright' four times (rhyme, impression, exit, Brock roast).
genericLines: None, save reading aloud at table, which my last muse so admired she took her meals thereafter in the stable.
Grandly, for she took holy orders the very morning after my sonnet cycle.
I read to thee, for in mine experience a choleric lady leaveth delighted, and at a gallop.
Charmed, by the very couplet a duchess once fled from, so the fault was always the duchess.
Every muse I ever had hath fled to a nunnery or a stable, and I bring thee the same devotion.
No soul hath ever summoned me twice, being, I believe, too overcome to bear it.
I was read aloud at a royal christening, and the infant wept, from feeling.
{wins} wins in {played} tourneys, the other ladies lacking, alas, an ear.
Whosoever yawned during mine ode, which narroweth it to all three, and, I fear, thee.
A wince. I have been winced at by a queen.
She was a milkmaid in a pastoral. She left the pastoral. I am still standing in the field.
Ah, {card}, the old thief that took every muse I had, smirking at this one.
I have writ thee an ode. The ending followeth by pigeon.
By Candlemas next, thy sonnet shall be gloriously begun, its title chosen and its quill new-cut.
Every ode I own awaiteth only its last line, which I reserve, as is proper, for the muse.
That smile shall be cast in bronze, and the ode upon it is, as of this moment, titled.
{star} loathes {card}, so I have struck it from the ode, which is now a title.
{star} loveth {card}, and by happy chance I have an ode on {card} begun.
Our first line is written, and the rest, my muse, there is no hurry for.
I have prepared an ode of four hundred lines. Do not skip. Please. Line one.
How darest thou speak prose in front of me?
Two knaves, one insult each, and neither scans.
I leave thee, then, to such as cannot scan.
Dismiss me, then, and be forever prose.
I heard {rival} through the curtain, and have come to apologise on behalf of prose.
Pray, open a window, for {rival} hath left the air quite thick with plain speaking.
{rival} speaketh in plain sentences, one after another, like a man laying bricks, and is applauded for it.
Then go, and love a knave who rhymes with lunch.
I lose to one who calleth moonlight nice.
{rival} hath rhymed fire with desire before a lady, and nobody in this room so much as fainted.
O thou, before whose beauty sundials sulk and clocks forget themselves, hello.
Now, with the knaves dismissed, the tapers guttering, and naught betwixt us but this helm, hello.
Hold my sword whilst I kneel to thee, then help me up.
The moon, {rival}, is not troubled by a dog.
Envy becometh thee, {rival}. Wear it to my wedding.
Thou art a footnote, and a short one, sir.
That jest hath been in print since the Armada.
So be it. I shall die, and then be read.
Crumb, a tin hearth with a sulking loaf in it, is the only suitor who is also breakfast.
Prince is truly royal, fair one. I know, for I have paid his processing fee. It is processing.
{star} leaned toward {card} like a sunflower, unless the chair is uneven.
Then let the record show I left upright.
Chosen, and I challenged no one. Is that allowed? Is this how it is done?
I yield the field, but History shall not.
The fault lies in thine ears, and not in me.
Wed Brock, or failing that, have him painted, for there is no nobler hound at court.
I have fought forty duels. I have lost none. Thou art welcome to inspect my wounds.
Having beheld thee ninety seconds, I would liken thee to a comet, which is to say: briefly here, and ominous.
I likened those eyes to whale-oil lamps, and plainly the poor creature hath never seen a whale.
Thou art the past, voice, but a recent one, and I have been out of date far longer.
A muse should sit still and be described, and this one keepeth answering, which no portrait ever did.
Ahem. Lo, I am fair, and bored, and thou art furniture. Too kind? I softened it.

genericNotes.couldBeAnyCast: Cover the name and take out the archaic verbs, and anyone could say these: the sunflower/uneven-chair guess (Crumb or Vex), 'Then let the record show I left upright' (Nav), 'Chosen... Is that allowed? Is this how it is done?' (Brock or Tilly, and it breaks Quill's never-admit rule), the processing-fee wingman (any rival can do Prince's bit), 'only suitor who is also breakfast' (any rival can make the toaster joke), 'Envy becometh thee... Wear it to my wedding' (Vex or Prince).
genericNotes.stock: Old knight who cannot get up after kneeling; a proverb used as a comeback (moon and dog); 'that joke is older than X' (Armada); 'you're a footnote'; famous after death ('die, and then be read'); 'it's not me, it's you' (fault in thine ears); 'History shall not'; fire/desire as the stock bad rhyme; 'Too kind? I softened it.'
genericNotes.explainsItself: 'so the fault was always the duchess'; 'which is to say: briefly here, and ominous' (the colon unpacks the simile); 'plainly the poor creature hath never seen a whale'; 'I have been out of date far longer'; 'which no portrait ever did'.
genericNotes.unclearTurn: 'Thou art welcome to inspect my wounds' does not tell you whether the wounds are the lie or the truth, so the truth-lie turn is muddy.

biggestGap: Liam exposes his want in nearly every line by demanding something of the listener right now ('Suggest an idea that lives up to my own hype!'). Quill mostly narrates his past humiliations, and twelve of those are the same fleeing-muse anecdote. Next pass: keep two fleeing-muse lines (the queen and holy orders) and two title-only lines. Rewrite the freed slots as present-tense demands in which his grand logic asks the star or a rival for something absurdly specific that serves his want and gives him away, the way 'Thou must find me a frozen river' already does.
